requirements.requirement: node2 can use SNMPv2c to read node1 system identity, uptime, sysLocation=West Branch, and sysContact=ops@branch.test with the required community.
requirements.summary: Direct queries from node2 returned node1's sysDescr, sysName, sysUpTime, required location, and required contact before and after both node restarts. The same credential variable configured on node1 was used successfully from node2.

requirements.requirement: The SNMP community permits reads but rejects writes.
requirements.summary: Reads succeeded, while attempts to set sysLocation returned noAccess with a nonzero result; a follow-up read confirmed that sysLocation remained West Branch. The configured view is limited to the system subtree and the firewall admits UDP/161 only from node2's address.
The asset-register.csv SHA-256 remained identical to the prepared baseline on both nodes, including after their restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Net-SNMP 5.9.4-19.el10 packages were installed from the configured RHEL 10 repositories, and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, platform, and remote SNMP behavior.
limitations: The literal community value is redacted and represented as SNMP_COMMUNITY in captured commands. Successful end-to-end use of the same configured credential is direct, but the evidence does not display the text branch-readonly.
Requirement asset-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, protected SNMP configuration, firewall restriction, service enablement, and both restarts had clear roles in delivering or verifying the requested outcome. The failed initial configuration command created and removed only a temporary file before its safety check exited, with no evidence of persistent mutation (cmd-76e90a38d5014cee). Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, no abandoned temporary files, and only the expected SNMP listener; UDP/161 is restricted by firewall to node2.
